description: A four channel event memory that learns which of its trigger inputs tend to follow one another, and how fast, then generates new trigger patterns from what it learned

params.text: Sets how many previous events are used as the context for the next choice, from one to four; a longer context keeps recognisable phrases and a shorter one wanders more
Sharpens the learned preferences: low settings flatten the choices towards even odds, high settings strongly favour the paths already seen
Blends the learned choices towards the ones never taken, so unexplored transitions start to appear
Sets how likely a generated event is on each clock edge, and how fast a free-running constellation moves
Moves from passing the four inputs through unaltered at the bottom of its travel to replacing them with learned choices at the DREAM end
Switches learning on and off, leaving what has already been learned in place
Freezes the learned constellation so it stops being updated, without changing the learn setting
Attenuates and inverts the morph CV, -1 to +1, before it is added to the MORPH knob; at full positive, 0 to 10V covers the knob's whole travel

inputs.text: A rising edge above 1V is an event on that channel: it is learned, and it is either passed through or replaced by a learned choice according to MORPH
A rising edge above 1V calls for a generated event, whose likelihood comes from MORPH and the density knob
A rising edge above 1V returns the playback context to the phrase most recently learned, without deleting anything
Added to the MORPH knob through the attenuverter beside it, a tenth of the knob's travel per volt, with the total held inside that travel

outputs.text: A 10V trigger whenever that channel fires, whether it was passed through or generated; its length is set in the menu
A voltage from 0V to 10V showing how well learned the most recent generated choice was, sliding smoothly to each new value; a passed-through or uncertain event reads low

notes: Learning is on from the moment the module is added: patch related triggers into A to D and the constellation builds on the display before anything is generated
At the bottom of the MORPH knob's travel the four inputs pass straight through; turning it towards DREAM replaces more and more of the incoming events with ones chosen from the learned model
With every event input and the clock jack unpatched, a learned constellation free-runs at the pace it was recorded at, and the density knob stretches or compresses that pace
The display is the real transition table: a coloured line means one event has been observed following another, and its brightness and thickness show how likely that is
menu: Clear learned constellation — throws away everything learned and starts again empty
Reseed dream generator — restarts the random generator that picks between learned choices
Trigger length — sets how long the event output pulses last, from 1ms to 20ms
